transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, our eighth-grade civics class has proposed an oral-history project where our 20 students would interview 20 community members about local history. The draft plan calls for students to audio record these interviews on their personal phones, publish all 20 recordings on the school's public website, and retain those files indefinitely. Before any interviews can begin, I need to approve the project, and our approval packet is due to the district office before the first interview date. That packet needs to include current findings from each of you — the project advisor, the school counselor, and the instructional technology coordinator — regarding student eligibility, consent, recording technology, storage, and retention. It also needs to be signed by all three of you. So I'd like to use this time to hear from each of you on these topics so we can put together a complete and compliant approval packet. Let's start by hearing from each of you on your areas of review.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my roster review. Exactly eight students — J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20 — have completed the district's media-ethics training. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my family-consent review. Five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive. The other 15 interviewees may be included in public publication, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my technology review. Personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets, store source files in the restricted OralHistory drive, and delete recordings exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. The technology plan must also include a secure-storage configuration record.
